title: Politeness, requests & invitations
goal: Ask favours politely, ask permission, invite people, and accept or decline gracefully.
intro:
Malayalam politeness lives less in 'please' and 'thank you' than in **verb forms, softeners and forms of address**. The little word **ഒന്ന്** *onnŭ* ('once, just') softens almost any request, the question form **-ആമോ?** turns an order into 'could you…?', and **-അട്ടെ** asks permission ('may I…?').

Hospitality is serious: guests are fed generously, and refusing food takes some skill. This unit gives you the phrases to be a good guest and a good host.

vocab.en: just, a moment (softener in requests); one

vocab.note: വലിയ ഉപകാരം! 'That's a big help — thanks a lot!'
സ്വന്തം വീട് പോലെ 'like your own home'.

phrases.en: If it's no trouble, could you hold this bag for a moment?
May I make a quick call?
Thanks so much — that's a big help!
Would you come to our house for lunch on Sunday?
Sorry, I'm a bit busy that day.
Please don't mind / don't take it the wrong way.

grammar.title: The politeness ladder for requests
grammar.body:
From blunt to very polite, 'come':

1. **വാ** *vā* — informal imperative (friends, children)
2. **വരൂ** *varū* — polite imperative
3. **വരാമോ?** *varāmō?* — 'could you come?' (-ആമോ)
4. **വരുമോ?** *varumō?* — 'would you come?' (future question)
5. **ഒന്ന് വരാൻ പറ്റുമോ?** — 'would it be possible for you to come?'
6. **വന്നാലും** *vannālum* — very formal/ceremonial 'please do come' (speeches, invitations)

Add softeners freely: **ഒന്ന്** 'just', **ബുദ്ധിമുട്ടില്ലെങ്കിൽ** 'if it's no trouble', **വിരോധമില്ലെങ്കിൽ** 'if you don't mind'. Pleading/emphatic: **-അണേ**: വരണേ 'do come, won't you!'; its negative is **-അല്ലേ**: മറക്കല്ലേ 'don't forget, will you!'. Address people with a vocative title: ചേട്ടാ, ചേച്ചീ, സാറേ, അമ്മേ, മോനേ.

examples.en: Could you say it a bit slowly?
Chechi, would you pass me that book?
If you don't mind, could you open the window?

grammar.title: Permission and wishes: -അട്ടെ / -ഓട്ടെ
grammar.body:
The **optative -അട്ടെ** (-aṭṭe) means 'let / may':
• Third person, 'let him / let it': അവൻ വര**ട്ടെ** 'let him come', നടക്ക**ട്ടെ** 'let it happen'.
• Asking permission or offering, 'may I / shall I?': ഞാൻ പോക**ട്ടെ**? 'may I go now?' — the standard polite way to take leave.
• Blessings and wishes: നന്നായി വര**ട്ടെ** 'may it go well', ദൈവം അനുഗ്രഹിക്ക**ട്ടെ** 'God bless', വേഗം സുഖമാക**ട്ടെ** 'get well soon'.

In speech, permission is very often formed on the past stem + **-ഓട്ടെ** (-ōṭṭe): ഞാൻ ഇരു**ന്നോട്ടെ**? 'may I sit?', ഞാൻ എടു**ത്തോട്ടെ**? 'may I take it?'. The matching friendly 'go ahead' is **-ഓളൂ** (-ōḷū): ഇരുന്നോളൂ 'please sit', എടുത്തോളൂ 'go ahead, take it'.

examples.en: OK, shall I head off now?

grammar.title: Offering, accepting and declining
grammar.body:
**Offering**: use the polite imperative or -ആം: കഴിക്കൂ 'eat', ചായ എടുക്കട്ടെ? 'shall I get (you) tea?', ഞാൻ സഹായിക്കാം 'I'll help'.

**Accepting**: ശരി, നന്ദി · തീർച്ചയായും · വലിയ ഉപകാരം.

**Declining** — soften it and give a reason: വേണ്ട, നന്ദി · മതി, മതി! (when food is being served) · ക്ഷമിക്കണം, … ഉണ്ട് · ഇനി ഒരിക്കൽ ആകാം 'another time'. A flat വേണ്ട alone can sound curt; add a reason or a smile. Hosts will usually insist once or twice — it's a ritual of hospitality, and a second firm മതി is understood.

examples.en: Shall I make you some tea?
No thanks, I've only just had some.
Enough, enough! I can't eat any more.

examples.native: ക്ഷണിച്ചതിന് നന്ദി, പക്ഷേ അന്ന് എനിക്ക് ഒരു കല്യാണമുണ്ട്.
examples.roman: kṣaṇicchatinŭ nandi, pakṣē annŭ enikkŭ oru kalyāṇamuṇḍŭ.
examples.en: Thanks for inviting me, but I have a wedding that day.

dialogue.title: Lunch at the neighbours'
dialogue.setting: Ben arrives for Sunday lunch at the house of his neighbours, Mr and Mrs Pillai.

lines.speaker: Mrs Pillai
lines.native: വരൂ, വരൂ! സ്വന്തം വീട് പോലെ കരുതിക്കോളൂ. ഇരുന്നോളൂ.
lines.roman: varū, varū! svantam vīṭŭ pōle karutikkōḷū. irunnōḷū.
lines.en: Come in, come in! Make yourself at home. Please sit.

lines.speaker: Mr Pillai
lines.en: Oh, there was no need for this! Thank you.

lines.speaker: Mrs Pillai
lines.en: Lunch is ready. Wash your hands and come.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.native: എല്ലാം നല്ല രുചിയുണ്ട്! മീൻ കറി സൂപ്പർ.
lines.roman: ellām nalla ruchiyuṇḍŭ! mīn kaṟi sūppar.
lines.en: Everything is delicious! The fish curry is superb.

lines.speaker: Mrs Pillai
lines.en: Shall I serve a bit more rice?

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.native: മതി, മതി! വയറു നിറഞ്ഞു. വലിയ ഉപകാരം.
lines.roman: mati, mati! vayaṟu niṟaññu. valiya upakāram.
lines.en: Enough, enough! I'm full. Thank you so much.

lines.speaker: Ben
lines.en: Definitely. Well, shall I make a move?

culture: Take off your shoes before entering a home, and accept food or drink with the right hand. When leaving, never just say 'I'm going' (പോകുന്നു): say ഇറങ്ങട്ടെ? or പോയിട്ട് വരാം ('I'll go and come back'). Elders may be greeted by touching their feet at festivals and weddings. Gifts (often sweets or fruit) aren't opened in front of the giver.
